title: Hybrid tensor/pipeline parallel throughput harness for multi-GPU scaling and regression detection
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that validates multi-GPU throughput scaling across hybrid parallelism modes (tensor parallel + pipeline parallel). The harness must produce stable tokens/sec and p95 latency metrics, detect regressions automatically, and integrate into CI with daily runs and on-demand experiments.

Context: Existing throughput tests focus on pure tensor or pure pipeline layouts and fixed microbenchmarks. Product needs end-to-end inference throughput numbers (tokens/sec) across real model checkpoints, sequence lengths, KV-cache warm/cold states, and mixed-batch workloads to make reliable autoscaling and routing decisions. We also need a statistical regression detector for p95 latency and tokens/sec (historical baseline + alerting).

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run a configurable experiment template that sweeps: GPUs per shard (1..8), pipeline stages (1..4), tensor-parallel degree (1..8), batch sizes (1,2,4,8,16), sequence lengths (64,256,1024), and KV cache state (cold, warm).
- Produces end-to-end metrics: sustained tokens/sec (1m moving average), p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization per-card, host CPU and PCIe bandwidth, memory (peak and average), and token-level variance.
- Regression detection: automatically compares latest run to baseline window (last 7 successful CI runs) and flags >8% drop in tokens/sec or >15% increase in p95 as a regression.
- Outputs artifact bundle: run_id, prometheus-compatible metrics, aggregated CSV, flamegraphs for slow tails, and a short summary JSON for dashboards.
- CI integration: daily scheduled job and PR gate job. PR gate must run a smoke configuration (2 GPUs, short sequence) that fails the PR if a regression is detected.
- Alerts: Slack channel post (perf-alerts) for confirmed regressions with links to run artifacts, diff charts, and a suggested rollback model variant.

Approach:
1) Harness shim: containerized runner that orchestrates distributed launch via existing orchestration layer, collects GPU metrics (nvidia-smi, DCGM), and uses synthetic and recorded prompt workloads.
2) Workload library: seed with 3 model checkpoints (small, medium, large) representing common workloads; include a recorded conversational workload for KV-cache warm paths.
3) Metric aggregation: implement streaming aggregator that computes 1m moving average tokens/sec and tail latencies in-run; persist to S3-run-bucket and push summary to metrics-store.
4) Regression detector: simple compare-and-zscore algorithm with configurable thresholds and hysteresis to avoid flapping. Allow manual triage if detector is uncertain.
5) Visualization: lightweight Grafana dashboards and a stable per-route per-model chart for tokens/sec vs GPU count.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Running full experiments across all sweep combinations is expensive; will prioritize automated smoke and nightly sampled matrix runs.
- Measuring end-to-end tokens/sec is sensitive to network/overlay variance; mitigate by repeating runs and recording infrastructure-level metrics to normalize.

Next steps:
- Prototype harness runner and a smoke experiment (2 GPUs, TP=2, PP=1, batch=8, seq=256).
- Create baseline runs for the three seed checkpoints and store artifacts.
- Wire the PR gate smoke run into CI.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the harness and regression detection plumbing. Model kernel optimizations and kernel selection policies will be follow-up tickets to act on the regressions detected.
